correctness.rationale: Prime symmetry forces X+1 factor; after translation H(Y)=Q(Y−1), H(Y)≡Y^(p−1) mod p and H(0)≡p mod p², hence Eisenstein. The Newton polygon gives every shift-root valuation 1/(p−1). Laguerre L_p(−z)=sum C(p,k)z^k/k! yields a finite Pólya–Schur multiplier sequence, which applied r−1 times to (1+X)^p makes F_{p,r} real-rooted. Irreducibility gives simplicity; positive coefficients give negative roots, and reciprocity pairs them about −1. Differentiate Eisenstein H at a root: leading derivative val=(p−2)/(p−1), other terms ≥1; norm gives discriminant p−2 and unit via m^m (H(0)/p)^(m−1), correct sign. Independent exact Bareiss/Sturm calculations corroborate p=3,5,7 and r=3,4,5.

value.rationale: The exact factorization plus local splitting and discriminant unit for an infinite natural prime-index binomial-power family resolves mathematically meaningful algebraic and arithmetic properties; the root-location theorem is a complementary structural classification rather than an arbitrary finite computation.

final_claim: For odd prime p and integer r>=3, F_{p,r}(X)=sum_k C(p,k)^r X^k=(X+1)Q with Q reciprocal irreducible over Q and Q_p, simple strictly negative roots, tame ramification v_p(α+1)=1/(p−1), discriminant valuation p−2 and discriminant unit (−1)^((p−1)/2) mod p.
